_comment: Hand-verified Phase-1 layout truth. Every number here was read off the
printed page by a human, NOT copied from pipeline output — that is the
whole point. The previous baseline in test_pipeline.py was written from an
eyeballed layout that was never checked, and two of its numbers were wrong
in the direction that HID bugs: it asserted 18 staves on a 22-staff page,
which a phantom staff satisfied, and 3 bars in a 2-bar system.
Verified by Sean 2026-08-28 (beethoven-5 p.10, both systems; wtc p.6
system 2) and by an independent ink probe that scores columns of near-
solid ink across each staff's full 5-line span (wtc p.6, all systems).
The probe is deliberately not the detector: it shares no thresholds with
measure_extractor, so agreement between them is evidence, not tautology.

wtc-p5.source: IMSLP932182 Well-Tempered Clavier I, PDF page index 5 (printed p.6), 600 DPI
notes: System 2 has TWO bars, not three. The detector finds a third barline at
x=4476 where two stems align across the staves; no ink crosses the gap

beet5-p10.source: IMSLP984073 Beethoven 5, PDF page index 10 (m274/m288), 600 DPI
notes: A pocket score: 15.8px line spacing at 600 DPI. The wind staves are
printed lightly enough that their lines break into ~25 runs with gaps
up to 11 staff spaces, which is why they were missed entirely and why
their x-extents are still wrong (see known_gaps).

lamer-p25.source: IMSLP15420 Debussy, La Mer (orch. score), PDF page index 25 (printed p.168), 300 DPI
lamer-p25.verified_by: left-margin render, read part by part (Claude, 2026-08-28) — evidence/lamer-p25-margin-21-staves.png
notes: Counted off the margin: Gdes Fl., Pte Fl., Htb, Cor A., Cl., Bons,
Cors x2, Tromp., Tuba, Timb., Cymb., Harpe x2, 1res Vons Div. x2,
2ds Vons Div. x2, Altos, Celli, C.B. — 21 staves in one system.
The twelfth is Cymbales, printed as a SINGLE rule. Before one-line
staves were detected the page reported 20, and every staff from the
harp down carried a staff_index one lower than its true slot — the
harm is not the missing percussion part, it is the nine parts under
it being mistaken for their neighbours.

known_gaps.symptom: systems read as [1, 10, 11] instead of [11, 11], and bars as [7, 13, 15] instead of [14, 15]
known_gaps.cause_as_first_diagnosed: staff_detector._staff_x_extent returns the longest CONTIGUOUS ink run on the middle line, and on these lightly printed staves that run is a fragment. Measured then: staff 0's middle line spans 276..2633 in 28 runs, largest gap 175px = 11 staff spaces. The prescription was a far more generous BRIDGE.
known_gaps.actual_cause: The bridge was never the problem. The 28 runs were an artefact of the measurement: the reader sliced a fixed 2px band around the line's nominal row, and the printed line wanders further than that, so it left the band and came back. Re-measured with a band scaled to the staff (0.35 spaces) and a 3-of-5 line vote, the SAME staff is 2 runs with a largest gap of 0.3 spaces. The ink was there all along.
known_gaps.fix: staff_detector._staff_x_extent reads all five lines with a scaled band and a 3-of-5 column vote. beet5-p10 now matches this file on staves, systems and bars; the two xfail tests in test_pipeline.py that recorded the gap are retired.
known_gaps.lesson: A measurement taken through a broken reader describes the reader, not the page. '28 runs with 11-space gaps' was a fact about the band width.

known_gaps.page: mahler5-p10 (Mahler_5_.pdf page index 10, Edition Peters, 300 DPI)
known_gaps.symptom: 20 staves on the page, 18 detected — neither Gr.Tr. nor Kl.Tr.
known_gaps.verified_by: Sean-style margin read 2026-08-31 — both parts carry a printed label and a single printed rule with noteheads on it, between Pauken and Erste Viol.
known_gaps.first_cause_FIXED: Three lone rows were candidates — the Gr.Tr. rule (1857 px), the wavy trill line printed between the parts (1410 px) and the Kl.Tr. rule (1858 px). The clearance rule rejects every row in a tight cluster, so the trill took both real rules with it. Fixed by dropping cluster members far shorter than the longest before clearance is applied (SINGLE_LINE_CLUSTER_WIDTH_FRAC).
known_gaps.cause_as_first_diagnosed: Reported here as two separate problems, the second of which was WRONG: 'Kl.Tr. is refused by _has_the_rest_of_a_staff because the Erste Viol. staff begins 75 px below it.' The violin staff is not involved. Probing the gate showed it fires on k=-2, row 1743, run 1410 against a 929 threshold — which is the trill line AGAIN, two staff spaces above Kl.Tr.
known_gaps.actual_cause: One piece of ink, charged twice. The wavy trill line printed between the two percussion parts (row 1744, run 1410) first made the clearance rule reject the whole cluster, and then — once dropped as an interloper — reappeared in _has_the_rest_of_a_staff as evidence of a five-line staff under Kl.Tr. Fixed in two steps: interlopers are dropped from the cluster before clearance (SINGLE_LINE_CLUSTER_WIDTH_FRAC), and the rows so dropped are then passed to _has_the_rest_of_a_staff as `ignore_rows`, because a row already judged not to be a printed rule is not evidence of a staff.
known_gaps.verified: Mahler p10 now 20 staves with 2 one-line staves. Nine pages across Mahler, La Mer and Boléro all match hand-read counts; the phase-1 set is unchanged by the second step and lamer-p25 still matches its GT.
